heading: Where to Eat in Penticton
title: Where to Eat in Penticton | Okanagan Roam
description: Where to eat in Penticton: brunch, bakeries, lunch counters, lakeside patios, winery dinners, breweries, cocktail bars, cheap eats and vegan spots.
intro: Penticton sits between two lakes, and a lot of its food does too. This guide covers the whole day: diner breakfasts and crêpes, small-batch coffee and bakery bread, lunch counters, dinners worth booking, lakeside patios, and a strong run of breweries and cocktail bars. Most picks are in Penticton itself, with a couple of dinners up the road in Naramata.

Patios, winery restaurants and beachside spots often cut back their hours from November to April, so check each listing's hours before you head out. For the full list, see all {page:/penticton/restaurants|Penticton restaurants}.

sections.heading: Breakfast & brunch
sections.lead: From big diner plates to a French crêpe room.

items.name: Bench Market
items.text: a busy cafeteria-style breakfast and brunch spot with a market, and a handy stop before a day on the Naramata Bench. The gluten-free options are excellent, and dogs are welcome on the outdoor terrace.

items.name: Terry's Comfort Food
items.text: a classic, no-frills diner on Main St with enormous breakfasts like the King Omelette. Kids love the free jellybean machine.

items.name: Tootsies Diner
items.text: a vintage locals' favourite in the industrial park, with oldies playing, a retro record table and fluffy pancakes.

items.name: Creperie Ooolala Bistro
items.text: a tiny room where the staff speak French. Regulars say it feels like a trip to Paris, so let the staff guide your order.

items.name: Elma
items.text: a beachfront Turkish restaurant with a weekend brunch worth booking. It's just as good at dinner, when the charcoal octopus is the order.

items.name: Petrasek Bakery
items.text: an artisan bakery and café on Main St for fresh bread and pastries. The owners will likely know you by name after a visit or two.

items.name: One14 Coffee Co.
items.text: small-batch roasting inside a converted industrial complex. Reviewers rate the gluten-free oat cookie on its own merits.

items.name: South Main Market
items.text: a family-run grocery with a from-scratch bakery, voted Best Bakery in the 2026 Best of Penticton. Locals line up for the cinnamon buns and homemade pies.

items.name: soe cafe
items.text: an eclectic spot filled with pottery, with vinyl for sale. Order the matcha by day, or a natural wine if you stay into the evening.

items.name: BRODO Kitchen
items.text: a lunch-only soup and sandwich spot with a small menu. Order the soup and sandwich combo.

items.name: Il Vecchio Delicatessen
items.text: a much-loved Italian deli with huge, generously stuffed sandwiches. Staff are happy to help first-timers.

items.name: BaBa Express
items.text: Vietnamese, with banh mi that comes out crisp outside and soft inside. The salad rolls stand out too.

items.name: Buy The Sea Seafood
items.text: a simple takeout counter and seafood market, known for its white and red chowder. Eat a bowl, then pick up fish for dinner.

sections.heading: Dinner worth booking
sections.lead: For a longer meal, including two in Naramata. Our {page:/guides/okanagan-winery-restaurants|winery restaurants guide} has more dining rooms among the vines.

items.name: The Restaurant at Poplar Grove
items.text: the fine-dining room at Poplar Grove Winery, with a lake view. Gluten-free bread is available, and the team is good at anniversaries and milestone birthdays.

items.name: Gusto Ferrari
items.text: a small, cozy Italian deli and restaurant that makes everything from scratch. Order the homemade pasta or the wood-fired margherita pizza.

items.name: Chulo Tapas & Bar
items.text: Spanish and Mediterranean small plates in a small tapas bar. Reviewers single out the roasted duck; share a few plates with a craft cocktail.

items.name: Bistro Lapin Perdu
items.text: a quiet, romantic French bistro inside the historic Naramata Inn, with a garden view. Book it for an anniversary or a first date.

items.name: Terroir Kitchen
items.text: a quiet farm-to-table restaurant where nearly everything is locally sourced. The pace is unhurried, so settle in.

items.name: Salty's Beach House
items.text: right on Okanagan Lake. Order the ahi tuna salad or fresh oysters, and come for the late happy hour.

items.name: Hooded Merganser Restaurant
items.text: lakefront views and a salmon bowl reviewers love. Service can slow on busy nights, so pick a quieter evening if you can.

items.name: Sociale
items.text: a lake-view patio and a roadside bar that's good for people-watching. The happy hour is well loved.

items.name: Kitchen @ Da Silva Winery
items.text: the tapas restaurant at Da Silva Vineyards and Winery, with lovely views. It's known for the Chef's Choice tasting, fresh bread and paella.

sections.heading: Drinks
sections.lead: Penticton pours a lot of beer. See all {page:/penticton/breweries|Penticton breweries} for the rest.

items.name: Tin Whistle Brewing
items.text: the self-described original Okanagan microbrewery, in a former fruit cannery on Fairview Road. The Peach Cream Ale is always on tap, and records spin in the background.

items.name: Abandoned Rail Brewing Co.
items.text: solid beer and real food, with a gluten-free cauliflower-crust pizza and GF beer. The patio looks out toward the mountains, and dogs are welcome.

items.name: The Forest
items.text: a moody, design-forward cocktail bar. Its nightly Enchanted Hour comes with complimentary flatbread.

items.name: Wildflower Distilling Co.
items.text: a downtown distillery that doubles as an intimate cocktail lounge, using its own gins and vodkas. Start with a tasting flight.

items.name: OROLO Restaurant + Cocktail Bar
items.text: a steakhouse and cocktail bar at Chronos Winery. Regulars plan around the well-priced oyster happy hour.

items.name: Mykonos Pizza & Spaghetti House
items.text: a cheerful, self-serve Greek-Italian family restaurant. Regulars call it the best-value sit-down meal in town.

items.name: The Underdog
items.text: a no-frills bar where everything on the food menu stays under $10, with pool and darts.

items.name: Happiness Thai Restaurant
items.text: a small, takeout-only spot with a warm owner. Order the Tom Yum and watch for the generous lunch specials.

items.name: TacoRiendo Mexican Cantina
items.text: near Skaha Lake. Order the fish tacos or the enchiladas verdes, and browse the small attached grocery.

items.name: Angry Vegan
items.text: Penticton's oldest dedicated vegan restaurant, open since 2017, with a menu mostly made in-house from scratch.

items.name: Gratify
items.text: a vegan café and dessert shop whose gluten-free and vegan baking reviewers call excellent. Check the freezer for treats.

items.name: Stillfood Bistro & Cappuccino Bar
items.text: a fully vegan brunch bistro, and celiac guests can trust the gluten-free options too.

items.name: Theo's Restaurant
items.text: a cozy, traditional Greek room with timber beams and a wood-smoke feel. Order the vegan moussaka.
